title: PhD Cover Letter: Connect Your Experience to the Advertised Project
seoTitle: PhD Cover Letter: Structure, Evidence and Sample Wording
seoDescription: Write a PhD cover letter around the project's criteria, using real evidence, a practical paragraph plan and honest sample wording.
intro: A PhD cover letter connects your experience to a specific project. Choose a few relevant examples, explain what they show and follow the advert's instructions for length and supporting documents.
description:
A PhD cover letter connects your experience to a specific project. Choose a few relevant examples, explain what they show and follow the advert's instructions for length and supporting documents.

Choose evidence that fits the project

Read the essential criteria and identify two or three examples from your own work that address them. Describe the problem, your contribution and what you learned. A dissertation, laboratory project or software implementation can provide useful evidence when its methods connect directly to the advertised research.

Build a clear letter

Open with the vacancy title and your reason for applying. Use the middle paragraphs to connect relevant experience to the project, then explain the question or methods you would like to develop. Close with a concise statement of interest and the documents supplied. Follow the requested length rather than treating one page as a universal rule.

Edit for accuracy

A cover letter should complement the CV without repeating every entry. Remove vague claims about excellence and unsupported promises about results. Check the institution, supervisor, project reference and submission method. If the advert requests a different statement or no letter at all, follow those instructions.

An opening paragraph you can adapt honestly

An illustrative opening is: “I am applying for the doctoral position on [project]. My work on [actual project] involved [relevant method], and I would like to develop that preparation through the advertised research on [specific question].” The next paragraph should show the evidence behind the connection. Describe a decision, result or limitation from your work rather than repeating the advert’s adjectives. If you have not used a required method, explain related preparation accurately and distinguish it from what you hope to learn. Close by confirming the documents supplied through the requested route.

Read the selection criteria before writing the opening

A PhD cover letter should help the reader connect your preparation to the advertised research. Start with the vacancy reference and identify two or three requirements you can support with real evidence. A list of software names is less useful than an explanation of how you used one relevant method, what decision you made and what the result taught you.

Separate essential qualifications from desirable experience. If you do not meet an essential requirement, check whether equivalent preparation is permitted before presenting the letter as a solution. Where you meet the essentials but lack a desirable technique, acknowledge the training need briefly and point to relevant preparation. Do not claim proficiency because you have only read about a tool.

A paragraph plan for an advertised project

ParagraphPurposeEvidence to include
OpeningIdentify the application and research connectionExact project title, reference and a specific reason for applying.
PreparationShow how you have worked on a relevant problemOne project, your contribution and a method you can discuss.
Project connectionExplain how that preparation supports the vacancyA direct link to the advertised question and a realistic learning need.
ClosingComplete the application professionallyRequired attachments and any practical information the call requests.

Follow the stated length and upload instructions. If the portal asks specific questions, answer those rather than attaching a generic letter that repeats your CV. A letter for a research position should not become a full proposal unless the call explicitly requests that content.

Illustrative wording, with evidence left for you to supply

"I am applying for [project title/reference]. In my [degree or role], I investigated [specific problem] using [method]. My contribution was [task you completed], including [one decision or responsibility]. This experience prepared me to engage with the project's focus on [requirement stated in the advert]."

The next paragraph might say: "I would bring experience in [supported skill] and would need further training in [relevant method]. My work on [actual example] gives me a starting point for that training. I am particularly interested in the project's question about [accurate topic], rather than assuming a particular result in advance."

These paragraphs are a framework, not a finished applicant's history. Replace every placeholder with something true and remove any sentence that does not fit your experience. Do not invent a numerical result to make the letter look stronger. A clear description of a real responsibility is better than a fabricated improvement percentage.

Edit the letter against the rest of the application

Check that dates, project titles and qualification names agree with the CV and forms. If you describe work as collaborative in one document, do not present it as entirely independent in another. Use the same status for outputs everywhere: a draft, preprint, submitted manuscript and published paper are different things.

Read the letter aloud once. Replace sentences you would struggle to explain in an interview. Remove broad praise of the institution unless it identifies something relevant to the work. The final letter should make it easy for the reader to understand why your evidence belongs beside this project's requirements.

Should I explain every weakness in the letter?

Address a relevant issue briefly if the application needs it. Do not turn the letter into a defence of your entire record. Use the designated contextual-information section where one exists, and keep the research evidence easy to find.

Can I reuse a previous cover letter?

Reuse accurate background facts, then rebuild the connection to the new project. Check every institution name, vacancy reference, research topic and attachment before submitting.

Make the final paragraph useful

Close with the practical information requested by the call, such as the attached documents or availability for the stated interview process. Avoid using the ending to repeat every achievement. If your degree is ongoing, state its accurate status rather than describing yourself as already graduated. If a proposed start date matters, distinguish your availability from immigration or other approval that remains outstanding. Check that the recipient, project reference and filenames match the final application. A careful ending helps the reader process the letter; it does not need a promise that you will exceed every expectation.

Official sources and further reading

Requirements and policies should be checked for your programme and application date. Sources checked on 19 October 2026.

  • Oxford Careers: academic applications
